subject: SOC 2 recert: evidence escrow & extended retention + capacity uplift request
messages:
From: Danielle King <danielle.king@escrodata.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@escrodata.com
Date: 2026-08-30T14:12:00Z
Subject: SOC 2 recert: escrow & retention ask

Hi Connor —

We kick off our SOC 2 recert in mid-October and our auditors have asked for two things I wanted to surface early:

1) Evidence escrow: legal is requesting that a snapshot of the SOC 2 evidence bundle (control docs, supporting logs for the audit window) be placed in a secure escrow for the duration of the audit in case we need independent review.

2) Retention exception: we need audit logs retained for 24 months (your default is 12 months). Can Redwood support a temporary retention extension for the audit window (plus a 30-day validation period)?

3) Temporary capacity uplift: during our evidence run and vendor interviews we expect elevated API traffic. Can you provision a short-term burst to cover ~2x our current committed throughput (est. 100k tokens/min) for 2 weeks?

Please let me know what process you need (NDA, amendment, PO) and any lead times or cost estimates. I can loop in procurement/legal if helpful — attaching our standard NDA and the auditors' evidence checklist.

Thanks,
Danielle King
Head of Compliance, EscroData Inc
Attachment: escrow-NDA.pdf
Attachment: escrodata-audit-checklist.xlsx

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Danielle King <danielle.king@escrodata.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-30T16:05:00Z
Subject: Re: SOC 2 recert: escrow & retention ask

Thanks Danielle — appreciate the heads up. We're happy to help get this scoped so your auditors have what they need. Quick reaction and next steps from our side: 

- Evidence escrow: we have two workable patterns: (A) direct escrow to a mutually approved 3rd-party escrow provider, or (B) a time-bound, access-restricted secure share of the evidence in our customer portal with enhanced access logging and a notarized certificate of transfer. Option B is typically faster to stand up. Either approach will require an NDA + specific access policy.

- Retention extension: we can support a 24-month retention window as a contract addendum with a storage surcharge. We will need the effective dates and whether you want it applied retroactively to prior logs or only going forward.

- Capacity uplift: we can provision a dedicated burst pool for the 2-week window. I'll have a pricing/lead-time estimate. Generally we need 5 business days to reserve the GPUs for a guaranteed burst.

Attaching a short MAP template to capture milestones (auditor access dates, retention start/end, PO/PO terms). Kim and Karthik — can you advise on the proposed retention pricing and escrow options?

Connor O'Brien
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Attachment: MAP-template.xlsx

Subject: Re: SOC 2 recert: escrow & retention ask — technical options and cost guidance

Hi Danielle — copying our security + provisioning notes below so you have concrete options to present to legal/audit. Happy to jump on a 30-min call tomorrow to walk through.

Summary of feasible options:

Option 1 — 3rd-party escrow (longer legal runway)
- We produce a time-stamped evidence bundle (control artifacts, redacted support docs, audit logs) and transfer to your chosen escrow provider.
- Pros: legal separation, independent custody.
- Cons: additional integration + transfer time. Estimated timeline 7–10 business days after NDA.
- Estimated one-time fee: $5k–$8k for the bundle transfer (depends on volume).

Option 2 — Redwood-managed ephemeral escrow (preferred for speed)
- We create a time-bound evidence snapshot hosted in a restricted S3 bucket with customer-managed KMS keys, strict IAM access, and immutable access logs. We provide notarized transfer receipt and an auditor account with read-only, time-limited credentials.
- Pros: faster (2–3 business days), full access/audit trail in our portal, integrated with our existing retention controls.
- Cons: custody remains with Redwood, covered by our SOC controls and customer KMS.
- Estimated one-time fee: $2k–$4k plus storage surcharge (see retention below).

Retention exception
- We can extend retention to 24 months for the specified audit window. Pricing model: $0.03/GB/month surcharge beyond baseline retention. We'll provide an estimate once you share expected log volumes. Option can be retroactive if you provide the extension start date.

Capacity uplift
- Short-term dedicated burst (guaranteed throughput): lead time typically 5 business days. Cost: uplift priced as a committed two-week reservation + overage cap. Preliminary estimate: $6k for the two-week guaranteed uplift to the capacity you described.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Confirm which escrow option you prefer (1 or 2).
2) Provide expected log GB for the audit window (so we can price retention).
3) If you want the capacity uplift reserved, confirm start/end dates; we'll queue the reservation.

I'll draft the language for a retention addendum and an escrow clause for legal review once you choose an option.

—Kimberly Park
Customer Success (Security Lead), Redwood Inference
Attachment: evidence-escrow-options.pdf
